estimates.narrative: Policy momentum toward a 10-year ILR baseline under Earned Settlement is strong and supported by official documents, with implementation signals around April 2026 and a consultation process through February 2026. While there is near-term uncertainty due to exemptions and transitional arrangements, the direction and timing make May 2026 plausibly concurrent with the policy shift for many migrants.
summary: There is strong official momentum toward a 10-year baseline for settlement under an Earned Settlement framework, with formal proposals and consultations indicating this direction.
Implementation signals suggest changes could begin around April 2026, making a May 2026 effect plausible for many applicants.
Public consultation runs through February 2026, with final policy decisions following; this introduces near-term uncertainty about exact application by May 2026.
Exemptions and transitional arrangements imply non-uniform waits for different cohorts, potentially delaying full, uniform adoption for all migrants.
Overall trajectory is highly likely to move toward a 10-year baseline, though the exact scope by May 2026 depends on final decisions and transitional rules.

anchor.basis: Why this reference class and anchor probability were chosen: The reference class comprises official government and parliamentary proposals indicating a 10-year baseline for settlement under an earned settlement model, supported by multiple sources. question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Momentum toward a 10-year baseline (earned settlement) is strong, with official proposals and consultation implying a default 10-year ILR path.

Implementation is expected to begin around April 2026 with changes potentially taking effect by May 2026 for many migrants, but final enactment depends on consultation outcomes and parliamentary process.
Exemptions and transitional arrangements mean the 10-year baseline will not apply uniformly; some cohorts may qualify sooner under time-adjustments.
Political and practical uncertainty could push rollout beyond May 2026, tempering certainty of a full 10-year baseline by then.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections accurately highlight timing uncertainty and exemptions that temper near-term universality, but do not contradict the overall trajectory toward a 10-year baseline.
justification.adjustment: Slight downward calibration from 0.91 to 0.88 to reflect the non-guaranteed nature of enactment by May 2026 and the non-uniform application due to exemptions and transitional arrangements.

forecasts.reference-class: UK immigration policy reforms proposing a 10-year baseline qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain/settlement (earned settlement model), with exceptions and transitional arrangements.

sources.claim: GOV.UK states the default qualifying period for settlement would be ten years under the earned settlement model, with potential reductions based on contributions.

House of Commons Library notes that the May 2025 immigration white paper proposed raising the baseline from five to ten years, with some groups still able to qualify sooner; changes expected to begin in April 2026, subject to final decisions after consultation.
Commons Library briefing covers the 10-year ILR proposal and notes that the immigration rules will begin to change from April 2026; discusses the consultation and potential transitional arrangements.
Guardian reporting notes Labour proposals to increase the ILR eligibility period to 10 years as part of broader settlement reforms.
The default qualifying period for settlement would be increased from five years to ten years under the earned settlement model, with exceptions and a time-adjustment framework.

Migration Observatory analysis describing the proposed 10-year baseline and potential adjustments, noting the public consultation ongoing.
The GOV.UK consultation states that the default qualifying period for settlement will be increased to 10 years, with potential reductions based on factors like integration and contribution.

causal-factors.name: Anchor policy momentum towards earned settlement with a 10-year baseline
causal-factors.rationale: Official documents and summaries state the default baseline for settlement would be ten years under the earned settlement model, signaling strong policy momentum toward a 10-year ILR pathway. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement/a-fairer-pathway-to-settlement-statement-and-accompanying-consultation-on-earned-settlement-accessible))

causal-factors.name: Implementation timing set to commence from April 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Parliamentary and government sources indicate immigration rule changes, including the 10-year baseline, would begin to take effect from April 2026, increasing the likelihood the change appears by May 2026. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cdp-2026-0006/))

causal-factors.name: Exemptions and time-adjustments create non-uniform waits and limit the 10-year baseline for many cohorts
causal-factors.rationale: The earned settlement proposals include reductions (e.g., 5 years for high earners or volunteering, 3 years for Global Talent/Innovator; 15 years for health and care middle-skilled routes), meaning the 10-year baseline would not apply uniformly. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement/a-fairer-pathway-to-settlement-statement-and-accompanying-consultation-on-earned-settlement-accessible))

causal-factors.name: Transitional arrangements for existing migrants
causal-factors.rationale: Consultation and policy briefs indicate consideration of transitional arrangements to exempt or ease impact for some people already in the UK, which could temper the near-term effect by May 2026. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cdp-2026-0006/))

causal-factors.name: Policy uncertainty and final decisions post-consultation
causal-factors.rationale: While the framework is laid out, final policy decisions depend on consultation responses and subsequent decisions, introducing uncertainty about exact application by May 2026. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cdp-2026-0006/))

causal-factors.name: Official policy momentum toward a 10-year baseline (Earned Settlement)
causal-factors.rationale: The government’s Restoring Control white paper (May 2025) and the November 2025 earned-settlement consultation explicitly push to raise the baseline to 10 years, with implementation expected from April 2026. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/restoring-control-over-the-immigration-system-white-paper?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Implementation timeline around April 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Parliamentary briefings indicate immigration rule changes would begin around April 2026, making a May 2026 shift plausible if the policy is adopted. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cdp-2026-0006/))

causal-factors.name: Public consultation through February 2026
causal-factors.rationale: The earned-settlement consultation runs through February 2026, signaling a formal process culminating in final policy decisions that could take effect soon after. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement/a-fairer-pathway-to-settlement-statement-and-accompanying-consultation-on-earned-settlement-accessible))

causal-factors.name: Political/public opposition and uncertainty about speed of enactment
causal-factors.rationale: Analyses and commentary from IPPR and Migration Observatory flag substantial criticisms and potential delays or dilution of reforms, introducing downside risk to timely adoption. ([ippr.org](https://www.ippr.org/media-office/revealed-the-devastating-impact-of-10-year-process-endured-by-thousands-on-course-to-settle-in-uk?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Exemptions and category-specific adjustments (e.g., high-skilled illustrates faster routes; care workers longer in some cases)
causal-factors.rationale: Provisions for time-adjustments and targeted shortcuts (e.g., 5-year or 15-year baselines depending on occupation) mean the baseline will apply unevenly, yet the 10-year default remains central. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cdp-2026-0006/))

causal-factors.name: Fiscal/benefits design and costs (NRPF, higher charges) could constrain or shape adoption
causal-factors.rationale: The policy contemplates higher immigration charges and possible no recourse to public funds for settlers, plus broader welfare-access considerations, which could temper momentum or alter rollout. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/restoring-control-over-the-immigration-system-white-paper/restoring-control-over-the-immigration-system-accessible?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Earned settlement baseline: default 10-year period with potential reductions for contributions
causal-factors.rationale: GOV.UK states the default qualifying period for settlement will be increased to ten years, with reductions possible based on contributions (time-adjustment model). ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement/a-fairer-pathway-to-settlement-statement-and-accompanying-consultation-on-earned-settlement-accessible))

causal-factors.name: Implementation timetable signals: changes planned to begin in April 2026 after the public consultation
causal-factors.rationale: Commons Library briefing notes that changes are planned to begin in April 2026 and final decisions follow the consultation. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10267/))

causal-factors.name: Political momentum from Labour and others to raise ILR wait to 10 years
causal-factors.rationale: Guardian reporting indicates Labour proposals to raise the ILR wait to 10 years, bolstering momentum behind the policy. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/feb/22/reform-uk-ice-style-agency-end-leave-to-remain-zia-yusuf))

causal-factors.name: Group-specific exemptions and extended baselines (e.g., 15-year base for certain medium-skilled roles)
causal-factors.rationale: Proposals include a 15-year baseline for workers below RQF level 6 in the Skilled Worker category, reducing the impact for some migrants. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement/a-fairer-pathway-to-settlement-statement-and-accompanying-consultation-on-earned-settlement-accessible))

causal-factors.name: Transitional arrangements for existing pathways
causal-factors.rationale: The consultation contemplates transitional arrangements; exemptions may apply, potentially delaying full application before May 2026. ([commonslibrary.parliament.uk](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10267/))

synthesis: There is strong policy momentum toward a 10-year settlement baseline, and planned implementation around early 2026 makes May 2026 plausible for many migrants. However, exemptions, transitional provisions, and ongoing consultation introduce non-trivial uncertainty, so the final outcome by May 2026 remains high but not guaranteed.
